item.content:encoded:
I agree with both of the previous comments - while the main article charmed me enough for an upvote, this one really does make the O5 council looks incompetent for not figuring out what seems obvious to us civilian readers.

(Frankly, I'd much prefer it if this Document doesn't exist - the hints and vague clues in the main text is tantalising enough as it is already, and the idea of Manius Curius Ater being another of the dime-a-dozen "secret power behind the Throne" detracts from both the more conceptually more interesting image of "the body of Gaius Octavius offered before the spirit of Caesar Augustus", and the previously established backstory of Augustus explicitly dismissing all other advises in building his eternal Emperorship)
